parts:
I am not sure the following could help figure out why. 

The following code shows when an error like c++ exception (unknown reason) happens when using Rcpp. At least that is one place such an error happens.

library(Rcpp)
library(inline)

src <- '
  #include <Rcpp.h>
  NumericVector i(a);
  std::invalid_argument e("invalid argument msg");
  if (i[0] == 0)  throw e;
  throw 3;
'

fx <- cxxfunction(signature(a="numeric"), body = src, includes = '', plugin = "Rcpp", verbose = TRUE)
fx(1)
fx(0)

This is the whole output from running the above code. At the end of output, we can see the error message of c++ exception (unknown reason).

Error: invalid argument msg

From the above, we can see the whole function in C++ is added with BEGIN_RCPP andEND_RCPP. END_RCPP has the code outputting such as message and it defines in Rcpp as

#ifndef VOID_END_RCPP
#define VOID_END_RCPP } catch( Rcpp::internal::InterruptedException& __ex__ ) { Rf_onintr(); } catch( std::exception& __ex__ ){ forward_exception_to_r( __ex__ ) ; } catch(...){ ::Rf_error( "c++ exception (unknown reason)" ) ; }
#endif

#ifndef END_RCPP
#define END_RCPP VOID_END_RCPP return R_NilValue;
#endif

So I am just wondering if there is any possibility and what condition could trigue throwing something not a std::exception.

By the way, should we leave out the 'not' from the correct error message of variable identifier (name) may not be reserved word? 


Jiqiang

I do know which line of code might output the error message of "c++ exception (unknown reason)", but I still cannot explain why.  I will send more info to stan-dev.  

@Richard, could you please let me know the version of your c++ compiler?  Thanks.


Jiqiang 

On Fri, Jan 24, 2014 at 7:58 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
With your R script, I got the same thing as I got before.

I'm running the standard off-the-shelf RStan.

The only diff I could see in our sessionInfo() is
that you had a later Rcpp version than me.  So I
went and installed the later Rcpp and restarted.  Same
result as I got before.

At least that means it's not a general RStan problem,
not that it helps solve your issue.

One thought:  I'm using the R GUI --- are you using RStudio
or the command-line version of R?    If so, can you see if
it works in the R GUI in a new session?  Maybe we can
isolate where it's having a problem before asking for
help from those who know R far better than me.

- Bob
